title: Picrasma Candy
subtitle: If anything, it pleases the palate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is this the spot?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Sure as shooting.
The hallway looks identical to any other.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Look, these footprints.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: They're less than ten minutes old.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But where's the door to room 707?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can sense some energy fluctuations nearby, but they're definitely not from arcane skills.
She presses her palm against the wall.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What else could produce such intense energy?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, can I help you with something?
The maid's voice comes unexpectedly from behind them.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Ms. Tuesday, I've got a question for you.
She stares intently at the maid, her gaze sharp as if she's finally caught the scent of her prey.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Do you know how to get to room 707?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Yup. What I've been looking for might just be in that room.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hmm. I'm usually more than happy to satisfy the requests of my guests, as long as it's within my power.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But this one crosses the line.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Shame. Looks like negotiations are over.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: And   thence   we   came   forth   to   see   again   the   stars.
After a brief moment, a glimmer of emerald light reignites in her eye.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Using arcane skills so frequently is bad for your eyes.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Didn't your family ever tell you that?
Her voice carries genuine concern.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So you knew what we were doing all along.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ha, of course. You weren't exactly subtle in your actions. What did you expect?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But you've reached your limit now.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Three.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What's that supposed to mean?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Two.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Tsk, screw this. Your mind games won't work on me.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: One.
The light in the mercenary's eye goes out in an instant.
Her eyes widen.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Huh? Who turned the lights off?
The hallway lights are as bright as ever.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: The lights are still on, dear.
Argus doesn't respond. She pulls a Picrasma candy from her pocket.
Her hands tremble slightly, causing it to slip from her grasp and fall to the floor with a clack.
She picks it up and places it back in Argus's hand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You rely far too much on Picrasma candy. It can't solve all your problems.
She tosses the candy into her mouth and chews it along with the dust from the floor.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: They usually work wonders for me.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Just one candy restores 50% of my vision. But in my line of work, 50% is never enough.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That's why I take two. I need my vision to be at least 100%.
She runs the candy along her tongue, and the expected sweetness fills her mouth.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That'll do the job most of the time, but sometimes I've got an extremely challenging task.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: That's when I eat a third candy. At that point, it's getting extremely dangerous.
She pops another candy into her mouth.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I should be able to see now.
No miracle occurs. Her eyes remain still, like a night sky with no stars.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Sh-Should I take more?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Absolutely not.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: The large amount of candy you've eaten is exactly why your eyes have failed you, and in such a crucial moment, no less.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Excess leads to destruction. This is true for all things. You'd do well to learn your limits.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I also had to be careful not to frighten those children too much.
The maid seems to relive some fond memories, a satisfied look on her pale face.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hmph. You've always put your faith in these candies, haven't you?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: One candy, 50% recovery; two candies, 100%; three candies, and you can tackle even the most insurmountable problem.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, how dependable they are! Just like the venerable Argus who succeeds in any job she takes on!
She chuckles.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: It's precisely your excessive confidence in these candies that has led to your marvelous destruction.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Just as the people's trust in you as a mercenary has led you to this bottomless abyss. Oh, you poor thing.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: And of course, they'd never have imagined this. Argus, the mercenary named after the hundred-eyed, all-seeing giant, is in fact a blind fool!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Who the hell are you?!
She fires in the direction of her voice, the gunshot ringing in their ears.
The bullet pierces the wall, and a strange wail echoes through the halls of the motel.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Damn it! Damn it!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hahaheh. Missed me.
She digs her fingers into her hand as she tries to control her trembling.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Uhn.
She steps forward, pushing her chest against the barrel of the gun.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: There you go. Now there's no way you can miss.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But do you have the guts to pull the trigger?
She tilts her head slightly, smiling.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: The decision's yours to make, but once I'm dead, you'll never find room 707.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Barbara, Kayla, everything you're looking for is all in that room, isn't it?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Don't you dare say her name with that filthy mouth!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But why? Ms. Kayla's such a lovely guest. I've very much enjoyed her company.
The maid looks at the mercenary's face with interest as it twists in rage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Enough.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You and I need to have a serious talk.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, there's no need for that.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Actually, my baby's eager to meet you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Your baby?
She looks at the bundle of swaddling cloth in the maid's arms.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Yes. In fact, the baby is the master of this motel.
She holds out the bundle.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I think the two of you ought to meet each other first. Here, hold it.
She places it in her arms. The bundle is much lighter than she expected—not the weight of a child.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is ...
She sees the carpet beneath her feet transform into a quagmire. Tuesday stands on top of the mud, smiling at her.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Vertin? Vertin!
The mercenary's shouts are dulled. It's as if she's been plunged under water.
She hears hurried footsteps approaching from a distance and feels the once-light bundle become as heavy as lead.
Something engulfs her ankles, pulling her down, down, down into a world of endless darkness.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Let go of it, Vertin!
An emerald flame struggles to light up, and the mercenary, lying on the ground, tightly grabs her hand.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I ain't letting our deal end this way! Not while I draw breath!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Argus ...

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Aaargh!
The maid presses her foot against Argus's fingers and steps down. Argus screams in pain.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Don't you interrupt them.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: There's no need to worry, Ms. Vertin. I've done this countless times.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Now, allow me to peer into your dreams.
